question: What is Pinewood Insurance's contract notice deadline?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract any statement about the contract notice deadline, notice period, termination or non-renewal notice requirements, renewal date, or contract end date, including the exact dates or durations mentioned and who stated them.
assumptions: Pinewood Insurance is a Renewal call (CALL-012), but call_types left empty because the question does not restrict to a call type.
'Contract notice deadline' is interpreted broadly to include notice periods, termination notice, and renewal or contract end dates.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Your current contract auto-renews with sixty days' notice, which means your notice deadline is the thirtieth of September.
findings.context: Pinewood's current contract auto-renews with sixty days' notice, making the notice deadline the thirtieth of September. — Stated by OrbitFlow's Account Executive Leo Grant in response to Graham's question about the current contract auto-renewing. Vendor statement about the customer's own contract terms.

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: Your renewal's on the twenty-ninth of November.
findings.context: The renewal date is the twenty-ninth of November. — Stated by OrbitFlow's Customer Success Manager Ruth Adeyemi at the opening of the call when explaining why she requested the meeting.

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.context: Customer Graham Attwood said he did not know about the notice deadline, which was three weeks away. — Customer reaction to the vendor disclosing the notice deadline; indicates the customer was previously unaware of the auto-renew and notice terms.

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.context: Graham Attwood stated he did not know the contract had the notice deadline. — Customer acknowledgement that he was unaware of the notice/auto-renew terms until disclosed by the vendor.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Which is why I've said it now rather than on the first of October. I'm not going to auto-renew you into a twelve-month contract you didn't intend to sign.
findings.context: Leo Grant said he disclosed the deadline early rather than on 1 October and would not auto-renew the customer into a twelve-month contract they did not intend to sign. — Vendor explanation of timing of the notice-deadline disclosure.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Serve notice, which stops the auto-renew, and then we negotiate the six-month option separately without a clock on it.
findings.context: Leo Grant advised the customer to serve notice by the thirtieth to stop the auto-renew, and offered a six-month option as a separate agreement. — Vendor recommendation on notice action; the notice deadline is restated as the thirtieth.

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.quote: So I need to serve notice by the thirtieth regardless, to keep my options open.
findings.context: Graham Attwood acknowledged he needed to serve notice by the thirtieth to keep options open. — Customer restating the notice deadline and intended action.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Then we have three weeks in October to agree the six-month terms, or you let it lapse on the twenty-ninth of November.
findings.context: Notice would be sent by email to the account contact, with exact wording and address supplied by the vendor, and lapse would occur on 29 November. — Vendor description of notice mechanics and the post-October timeline.

draft.answer: Pinewood Insurance's notice deadline is the thirtieth of September, per OrbitFlow AE Leo Grant, under a 60-day auto-renew notice term [C1]. The contract renews on 29 November [C2]. Customer Graham Attwood said he was unaware of the deadline and acknowledged he needs to serve notice by the thirtieth [C3]. Grant recommended serving notice and negotiating a six-month option separately, with notice sent by email [C4].

claims.text: Leo Grant (OrbitFlow Account Executive) stated that Pinewood's contract auto-renews with sixty days' notice, so the notice deadline is the thirtieth of September.
Ruth Adeyemi (OrbitFlow Customer Success Manager) stated the renewal date is the twenty-ninth of November; Grant also referred to lapse on 29 November.

Graham Attwood (Director of Operations) said he did not know about the notice terms, and the deadline was three weeks away at the time. He later acknowledged he needs to serve notice by the thirtieth to keep options open.

Grant disclosed the deadline early rather than on 1 October, saying he would not auto-renew the customer into a twelve-month contract they did not intend to sign. He advised serving notice by the thirtieth to stop the auto-renew and negotiating a six-month option separately. Notice would be sent by email to the account contact, with wording and address supplied by the vendor, leaving three weeks in October to agree the six-month terms.

not_covered: The contract clause itself or the year was not stated in the findings; the deadline comes from verbal statements on the call.
Whether notice was actually served is not shown.
